title.en: Keep discrete puzzles on integer cells

summary: Store piece positions as integer lattice coordinates and test placement by set occupancy rather than by geometry.
objective: Make a spatial puzzle exact so that fitting, collision and completion are decidable rather than approximate.
applies_when: Pieces occupy cells of a grid, tray, board or voxel volume.
Pieces are dragged, rotated or dropped into place.
Completion, overlap or legality must be decided.
intent_signals: detect when the tray is full
example_prompts: Build a voxel packing puzzle where pieces snap and overlaps are impossible.
Tell me when the tray is completely filled.
negative_signals: Continuous fitting problems such as jigsaw edges or physical stacking.
Free-form sandbox building where exact packing is not the point.
not_for: Continuous fitting problems such as jigsaw edges or physical stacking.
Free-form sandbox building where exact packing is not the point.

principles: A discrete puzzle is a combinatorial object. Once positions are floating-point, two pieces can overlap by a fraction, a tray can be almost full, and completion becomes a question of tolerance rather than of fact.
Occupancy sets make the important operations trivial and exact: overlap is set intersection, completion is set equality with the target region, and legality is a membership test.
Rotation of a lattice piece is itself discrete. Precomputing the distinct orientations of each piece avoids re-deriving them from rotated meshes and eliminates rounding at every rotation.

Snapping is presentation. It should show the discrete position the model already holds, not be the mechanism by which the model becomes discrete. A free-moving or explicitly invalid preview is a legitimate interface as long as the commit is discrete and validated.
implementation: Represent each piece as a set of integer cell offsets plus a placement, and derive the rendered transform from that placement.
Enumerate the distinct lattice orientations of each piece once and reference them by index during play.
Test placement by set operations against the occupied cells and the tray region, and report the specific conflicting cells.

Drive the drag interaction by projecting the pointer to a candidate cell and evaluating that candidate against occupancy and the board limits. The preview may show an illegal candidate, marked as rejected, or follow the pointer smoothly off-grid; what must stay discrete and validated is the committed placement.

Detect completion by comparing the union of placed cells with the target region together with the invariants that make the union meaningful: pairwise non-overlap and the piece-use rule. A union alone loses multiplicity, so either check those invariants at completion or rely on a placement path that has guaranteed them all along.
observable_checks: Attempt to place a piece one cell into an occupied region and confirm the model refuses rather than allowing a near-fit.
Rotate a piece through all its orientations and confirm the cell set matches the precomputed orientation exactly.
Fill the tray and confirm completion fires from the set comparison rather than from a visual check.
Drag rapidly and confirm no piece ends between cells.

creative_affordances: Non-cubic lattices, hexagonal boards and layered grids all work with the same discipline.
Physical-feeling drag, wobble and settle animations remain available over an exact model.
known_limits: Authored state-model guidance; no runtime puzzle has been exercised for this record.
It does not provide a solver or a difficulty measure.
